title: Surprise midnight release. Stompworks a Roguelike with mech building.
author: Mekkablood
selftext:
A classic revenge story with cel-shaded fully customizable mechs. Buy the right parts, take out the enemies, and don't die. 18 torsos, 14 sets of legs and 27 weapons, you retain the skins you unlock even after death, but not the parts. It's been a lot of fun making this, and I hope you like it.

[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5383780/Stompworks/?beta=0](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5383780/Stompworks/?beta=0)

It was made with Opus 5.5 extra high. No mcp's just had Opus do the models within a three.js environment. Started off with the first mech, then built parts from there, a basic level, then added the gameplay and it took a goosebumps book worth of prompts to make what you see here. Will be working on changing up the sound a little bit.

comments.author: Raspberry-Void
comments.body:
In its current state, there's 3 major things that limits the enjoyment of the game: 

1. Sound, as you have acknowledged, is very strange and serves to undermine the impact and weight of the combat  
2. By the second level I could afford the most expensive parts, so it dampened the interest to keep playing a bit knowing I had the best parts already (Which made the bosses VASTLY underwhelming to defeat)  
3. A lot of the battleground props (trees and cars come to mind) are indestructible which makes you bump into them and even getting stuck in the middle of combat.   
  
All in all, the game is enjoyable in a sort of arcade sort of way, and it is fun to put together your own Mech.   
  
Heatmanagement at the moment is completely a non-issue in the actual gameplay, I don't even know what happens when you overheat because it never happened.  Likewise there's an indication of different damage types but I really didn't notice any difference between them while playing. 

I think a very effective move on your end would be to implement upgrades on each part, downgrading their performance at first and letting the player boost their cooldown and damage by upgrading them. That also makes the player balance upgrading old parts vs buying new ones.

replies.author: Mekkablood
replies.body:
I appreciate your feedback.

Update: A patch has been applied to change how the overheat works, and elite parts cost.

1. I think the sound is fine and took awhile to get it at this state. I don't hear my subwoofer kick in when playing the newest Mechwarrior, yet I made sure this had a high a very high dynamic range. I'm an audiophile nerd who focused a lot on getting this right. Is it a little arcadey? Sure, but that fits the aesthetic. This wasn't meant to, nor do I have the budget to make it sound like Armored Core. I'm guessing you saw this on claude gamedev as that was pretty much the only place people where complaining about the sound. You can look at the profiles of a number of people in there who do nothing except complain about ai, and love to do it in ai spaces.
2. You have a valid point here, my thought was I didn't want to gatekeep the parts too much so players can get a feel of the variety, and decide what's best. I think another thing I got wrong was implying the orange weapons are the best, the purple ones may fit a persons playstyle better even though cheaper. I will look into not only changing this but adding more parts.
3. Just part of the game, the enemies are there to bombard you so you can't get to the pickups easily without moving around a lot. They want to pin you down to destroy you and obstacles add a wrinkle that helps them out.
4. Will be tweaking with the overheating, as its just there so certain weapons aren't too powerful with spamming them over again. it just adds a cooldown to your weapons.
